note.headline: SPY and QQQ rebound sharply, but trend, fear and breadth still say wait

summary.thesis: SPY rose 4.71% and QQQ rose 7.0% on Nov 23, a bounce off the 1-month lows they set on Nov 20. Both indexes are still below their 50-day and 200-day averages. Fear was high on the last stored reading, and breadth is 3%. The bounce has not changed the downtrend.
summary.decision: Stand aside for long-term buying and for swing trades. The market gate is still active.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 682.29 (its 200-day average) would end the tech downtrend. The VIX would also have to fall out of 'high' to clear the market gate. A QQQ close below 608.45 or an SPY close below 689.81 would set new 1-month lows.

note.happening: On Nov 23, SPY closed at 722.29, up from 689.81 (+4.71%). QQQ closed at 651.03, up from 608.45 (+7.0%). Both indexes had set their 1-month lows on Nov 20. Even after the bounce, both are lower over the past 5 days (SPY -2.39%, QQQ -1.62%) and the past 20 days (SPY -5.63%, QQQ -8.59%). SPY is 6.9% below its 1-month high of 772.31 and QQQ is 11.5% below its 1-month high of 725.61, both set Oct 28. The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. No news is stored since the last note, so DATA does not say what caused the bounce.
note.business: The three readings agree, even though the price jumped. Trend: both indexes are below their 50-day and 200-day averages, which DATA classes as a downtrend. SPY is closer to recovering its long-term line: it is 1.1% below its 200-day average of 730.47. QQQ is 4.8% below its 200-day average of 682.29. Fear: the latest stored VIX is 35.89 (Nov 20), in the 'high' band (30+). That is the top of its range over the past 252 readings, and it is up 16.59 points over 5 days. The Nov 23 VIX isn't stored yet, so the fear reading lags the bounce. Breadth: only 3% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. That means almost the whole market is below its short-term trend, not just a few large names. As general knowledge, sharp one-day rallies often happen inside downtrends, and one rally by itself does not reverse a trend. Together the readings describe a market that bounced inside a downtrend, not a market that has turned up.

worth.text: No valuation is in DATA. The levels in this note mark price trends only.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: The rebound was large: QQQ rose 7.0% and SPY rose 4.71% in one day, and both are now above their Nov 20 lows (QQQ 6.5% above 608.45, SPY 4.5% above 689.81).
SPY is 1.1% below its 200-day average of 730.47. That is the nearest trend line for either index to reclaim.
The VIX reading of 35.89 is the highest of the past 252 readings. As general knowledge, very high fear readings have sometimes come near market lows, though that is not a rule.
bear: Both indexes remain below their 50-day and 200-day averages. QQQ is 9.0% below its 50-day average of 709.73, so tech setups keep failing the pipeline's market check.
Breadth is 3%, down from 12% in the previous note. Very few stocks are in short-term uptrends.
Fear is in the 'high' band, and the market gate also requires the VIX to leave 'high'. The latest stored reading is still from Nov 20.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average and the market gate. A close above it ends the tech downtrend. The VIX also has to fall out of 'high' to clear the gate, and that would support a selective stance.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.

longterm.why: QQQ closed at 651.03, below its 200-day gate of 682.29. Fear was 'high' as of Nov 20, and breadth is 3%. All three readings argue against new buying until QQQ closes above 682.29 and the VIX leaves 'high'.

swing.why: QQQ is 9.0% below its 50-day average of 709.73. Below that level, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check, and a one-day bounce does not change that.

decision.timing: Two releases are due Nov 25 at 08:30. One is the second estimate of Q3 GDP and corporate profits. The other is October Personal Income and Outlays, which includes PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation measure. The fear reading here is from Nov 20 because the Nov 23 VIX isn't stored yet. The nearest levels to watch are SPY 730.47 above and 689.81 below, and QQQ 682.29 above and 608.45 below.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 682.29 together with a VIX reading below 30 would clear the market gate and support moving from 'stand aside' to 'selective'. A QQQ close above 709.73 would be the cue to lean in more.
A QQQ close below 608.45 or an SPY close below 689.81 would set new 1-month lows. The Nov 23 bounce would then have failed and the decline would be continuing.
note.what_changed: In the previous note (Nov 20), both indexes had just set new 1-month lows. On Nov 23 they bounced sharply: SPY rose 4.71% to 722.29 and QQQ rose 7.0% to 651.03. Fear rose from 'elevated' (Nov 19 reading) to 'high' (Nov 20 reading of 35.89). Breadth fell from 12% to 3%. The 1-month lows reset to the Nov 20 closes, 689.81 for SPY and 608.45 for QQQ. The QQQ gate moved from 682.07 to 682.29. The stance stays 'stand aside'.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Tesla at 385.46 after an 11.46% jump with no news; margins shrinking, still avoid

summary.thesis: The 11.46% jump to 385.46 came with no reported news. Meanwhile quarterly sales are flat, margins are falling and free cash flow has dropped. The stock now trades near the top of its own valuation history.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: wait, because the price sits just below a resistance zone (a level where sellers have stepped in before) and the trend is still marked as down.
summary.act_at: Long-term, re-examine near 293.94 only if margins recover. Swing, act only on a close above 404.4 or a pullback that holds 363.89–368.73.

note.happening: Tesla closed at 385.46, up 11.46% on the day. There is no news since the last note to explain the move. The price is now close to its 20-day average of 384.49 and above its 50-day (376.17) and 200-day (381.53) averages, but all three averages are flat and the overall trend is still marked as down. The next earnings report is due on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Today's jump changes the price, not the business. The latest filed quarter (ended 2026-09-30, filed 2026-10-22) shows that sales growth stopped. Sales were down 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) over the last 12 months fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. Two filing-based warnings point the same way. Inventory is up 15% while sales are up 0%, and unsold cars can force price cuts. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, down from 33¢ three years ago. At risk: margins and cash generation if inventory forces discounts. Not at risk: the balance sheet. Tesla has 37.5B of net cash (cash minus debt) and 45.4B of liquidity, so funding is not a problem. The fear in the wider tech market noted by the macro view affects sentiment only. It does not change demand or margins.

worth.text: The two valuation methods give very different answers. A discounted cash flow model (DCF: today's value of the cash the business is expected to produce) puts fair value at 20.01 to 44.3, with a base case of 24.66. That is because it starts from only 3.3B of free cash flow. Even if growth starts at 30%, the DCF value is only 44.63. Tesla's own price-to-sales history (what investors paid per dollar of sales over 5 years) gives 203.8 / 293.94 / 399.81. At 385.46 the stock is near the top of that history, in the 63rd percentile of the last 5 years, at 14.7 times sales and 424.1 times trailing earnings. The filings note that the price needs about 51% a year growth, while the business delivered 3% a year over 3 years. So the gap between the methods comes down to one choice: value Tesla on its thin current cash flow, or on what the market has historically paid for its sales. Note: the data's valuation summary still quotes a price of 345.82, which is the 2026-11-20 options-chain price from before today's jump.
worth.key_assumption: With flat sales, the market keeps valuing Tesla at the low-to-middle part of its own 5-year price-to-sales range, not near the 399.81 top and not on its 3.3B of free cash flow.

bull: The balance sheet is strong. Tesla has 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity, so it can fund heavy spending without borrowing stress.
Sales over the last 12 months still grew, to 103.6B from 95.6B (8.3%), and analysts' next-year EPS (earnings per share) growth is 25%.

Options traders hold the most open call contracts at the 400 strike (14,601 open interest). Calls are bets on a rise, so some traders are positioned for the price to reach the 393.63–404.4 resistance zone.
bear: Quarterly sales fell 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago, while inventory rose 15%.
Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and 12-month free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B.
At 424.1 times trailing earnings, the price needs about 51% a year growth, against 3% a year delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the own-history high of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.66, so the jump made the stock more expensive, not cheaper.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.89–368.73), a level where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it would end this rebound.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine at this level only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Sales have stalled, margins and cash flow are shrinking, and the price is near the top of its own valuation history. The business is graded D, and the committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The price is in the 380.15–389.95 zone, just under resistance at 393.63–404.4 (touched 5 times), and the trend is still marked as down. No trade until a close above 404.4, or a pullback that holds 363.89–368.73.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report, the next test of margins, inventory and cash. The options-implied moves (14.2% by 2026-12-18, 22.1% by 2027-02-19) were priced on 2026-11-20 at 345.82, before today's jump, so they understate how far the price could move from here.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back toward the 15.78% seen two quarters ago.
Twelve-month free cash flow rises back toward 6.8B from 3.3B. That would lift the DCF values, which currently top out at 44.3.

The price falls to the 293.94 own-history midpoint while margins hold at or above 3.35%. That would revisit the long-term avoid. For the swing view, a close above the 408.62–417.44 resistance zone (touched 7 times) would revisit the wait.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid and wait. There has been no news since the previous note, which confirms the 11.46% jump to 385.46 is a price move with no business reason behind it.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA holds at 165.05 after 31% jump; fair value still hinges on margins

summary.thesis: NVIDIA's sales and cash flow are growing very fast, and the stock is cheap against its own history, but most of the gap to fair value depends on a record-high profit margin lasting.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term and make no swing trade for now: the price is stuck between support at 147.15–150.45 and heavy resistance at 174.23–180.81.
summary.act_at: Buy at 114.82; go to wait on a close below 147.15; swing entry only on a close above 180.81

note.happening: NVDA closed at 165.05, up 31.48% in a day. It is still in a downtrend, below its 50-day average (206.08) and its 200-day average (202.99). There has been no new news since the last note, and our data has no earnings date.
note.business: The business itself is very strong. Sales over the last twelve months reached 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Growth in the latest quarter sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters earlier. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (the cash left after spending on the business) rose to 127.0B from 72.0B, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. Analysts keep raising forecasts: next-year earnings per share (EPS) is now 16.61, up 27.7% in 90 days. Two risks could change the business. First, the margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and peaks like that usually fade. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while quarterly sales grew 106%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Two other things affect only sentiment or governance, not the business: insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set trading plans, and the price itself has been extremely volatile. The data has no segment breakdown, so we cannot say which product lines are driving growth.

worth.text: At 165.05, the stock trades at 20.8 times trailing earnings, 17.1 times this year's expected earnings and 9.9 times next year's. Its price-to-sales ratio of 13.1 is just below the peer median of 13.3, and it is at the very bottom (0.0 percentile) of its own 5-year range. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values a company on its future cash) gives 191.49 to 264.22, with 222.58 in the middle. The own-history price-to-sales method gives 217.35 to 411.04. The current price assumes free cash flow starts growing at about 22.0% a year. At 20% starting growth the model value is 152.77, and at 30% it is 222.58. The real swing factor is the margin. If operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 114.82, and at 32% it drops to 76.87. Note that the valuation summary text still quotes the old pre-jump price of 125.53.
worth.key_assumption: Operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, while free cash flow grows from 127.0B at a starting rate of about 20% or more.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B over a year, and the company holds 23.2B in net cash.
Next-year EPS estimates rose 27.7% in 90 days to 16.61, which puts the stock at only 9.9 times next year's earnings.
Price-to-sales of 13.1 is at the 0.0 percentile of its own 5-year history, and every valuation method puts the middle value at or above 222.58.
bear: Operating margin of 65.21% is at the top of its 5-year range; at a 48% margin the model value is 114.82, well below the price.
Unpaid customer bills grew 127% against 106% sales growth, which may mean sales were pulled forward.
The trend is down: the price is below the 50-day average of 206.08, with resistance at 174.23–180.81 tested 6 times.

levels.what: Bottom of the only support zone (147.15–150.45). A close below it would undo the recovery and move the call to wait.
The model value if operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 114.82, because that price already allows for a large margin fade.
The base-case cash-flow value. Trim near this level, where the price assumes the margin and growth the data already shows.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the committee says 'Hold'. The upside depends on a peak margin, and the risk from slow customer payments is still open, so hold rather than add.

swing.why: The price sits inside the 163.9–171.33 zone, with resistance starting close above at 174.23. A sensible stop under 147.15 is far below, so the risk outweighs the reward until the price pulls back into 147.15–150.45 or closes above 180.81.

decision.timing: Our data has no earnings date. The next quarterly filing will show whether the 65.21% margin and customer payments hold up. The options data is from 2026-11-20 and is priced off an underlying of 125.53, so its expected move is out of date.

change_mind: A close below 147.15 would turn hold into wait.
A next filing with operating margin back under 58.09%, or unpaid customer bills again growing faster than sales, would cut the fair-value range toward 114.82.
A close above 180.81 would clear the resistance tested 6 times and support a swing entry, with a stop under 174.23.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold, confirmed by the price staying at 165.05 inside the 163.9–171.33 zone and below resistance at 174.23, with no new news since the last note.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD rebounds 6.85% to 453.46, but still far above every fair-value estimate

summary.thesis: AMD's business is growing fast and getting more profitable, but at 453.46 the price assumes more growth than any of our valuation methods supports.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no entry while the price sits between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Value buy at 333.38 or lower; swing only on a close above 460.21

note.happening: AMD rose 6.85% to 453.46. That recovers part of the previous session's drop to 424.39. The price now sits just above the 424.03–451.0 support zone and just below the 460.21–480.33 resistance zone. The only news since the last note is a CNBC piece, reported, about what Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia means for AMD shares. The next earnings report is due 2027-02-02.
note.business: The rebound and the Nvidia headline change sentiment. They do not change the business. The latest filing (2026-11-04) shows a business in good shape. Trailing sales rose to 45.4B from 32.0B, up 41.87%. Last quarter's sales growth picked up to 44.68% from 37.85% two quarters earlier. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, roughly doubled to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, rose to 7.1B from 5.4B. AMD holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so its finances are not a concern. Analysts raised next-year EPS (earnings per share) estimates 11.3% in 30 days. Two things are at risk. First, inventory grew 57% while sales grew 45%; unsold chips can force price cuts. Second, the 18% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range of -2% to 22%. Margins at a peak often come down. Segment data is not available, so we cannot say which product lines drive growth. The competitive effect of Nvidia leadership news is not known from our data.

worth.text: Every method puts fair value well below the price. The cash-flow model (DCF), which values the business on its future free cash flow, gives 145.29 (bear), 186.22 (base) and 220.22 (bull). AMD's own history of price-to-sales gives 179.24 to 333.38. To justify the price, free cash flow would need to start growing at 55.7% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, which gives 186.22. At 20% it gives 129.23. Margins matter too: at a 13% operating margin, value falls to 98.25. Multiples tell the same story. The stock trades at 98.9 times trailing earnings and 16.4 times sales, versus a peer median of 10.7 times sales. It sits in the 88th percentile of its own 5-year price-to-sales range. The only multiple that looks reasonable is 25.7 times next year's earnings. That depends on analysts' next-year EPS of 17.64, which they expect to be roughly double this year's 8.08, coming true.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies 55.7% a year, while the model caps it at 30% (186.22 a share), so the gap rests on analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth holding up.

bull: Growth is speeding up: last quarter's sales rose 44.68%, up from 37.85% two quarters earlier.
Analysts keep raising forecasts: next-year EPS of 17.64 is up 11.3% in 30 days, which puts the stock at 25.7 times next year's earnings.
Cash is strong: free cash flow is 7.1B and AMD holds 8.7B more cash than debt.
bear: At 453.46 the price is above the top of every fair-value method (333.38).
Inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, a classic setup for price cuts and lower margins.
At 16.4 times sales, the stock costs more than the 10.7 peer median and sits in the 88th percentile of its own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 391.99–403.47 support zone. A close below it would mean the selloff is deepening, though the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range. The case for buying on value starts here.

longterm.why: The business is improving, but the price needs 55.7% cash-flow growth to make sense, well above the model's 30% cap. Wait for 333.38 or lower, or for results that support much faster growth.

swing.why: The price is boxed in between the 424.03–451.0 support and the 460.21–480.33 resistance. It sits above the 200-day average (431.01) but below the 20-day (505.19) and 50-day (552.3) averages, with no trend. The average daily range (ATR) is 45.95, larger than either distance, so no entry until a close above 460.21.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are more than two months away. Options price a 21.3% move by 2026-12-18, and put open interest outweighs calls 2.42 to 1, with the most puts at the 400 strike. More AI-sector or Nvidia headlines could move the price to either zone before the report.

change_mind: A close above 460.21 would show buyers taking the resistance zone and would open a swing entry toward 480.33.
A drop to 333.38 or lower while analysts' next-year EPS stays near 17.64 would turn the long-term call to buy.
If the 2027-02-02 report shows inventory still rising faster than sales (57% vs 45% now) or operating margin falling from 17.72%, the call would move to avoid even at lower prices.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait; the 6.85% rebound to 453.46 moved the price further above the 333.38 top of fair value, not closer to it.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Amazon rises 3.47% to 255.39 amid reported AI deal; still waiting for 238.65

summary.thesis: Amazon's margins are improving, but it is burning cash and its sales growth is slowing, and at 255.39 the price is already in the upper half of its own fair-value range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no trade, because the price sits in the middle of a range with resistance just above it.

note.happening: The stock rose 3.47% to 255.39. That put it back near its 50-day average of 255.07 and inside a price zone of 251.93–258.08. Several outlets reported that Amazon is buying the AI start-up Decart for $7.5bn, to gain its chip-software technology as Amazon prepares to sell its Trainium chips. Amazon has not confirmed the deal in a filing. There is no earnings date in the data, and one headline reported that the Nasdaq is 'in freefall'.
note.business: The things that change the business point in two directions. Margins are improving: operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. Cash is the problem. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) over the last 12 months was -46.9B, down from +10.6B a year earlier. Net debt is 66.7B (net cash of -66.7B). Demand is cooling: quarterly sales growth was 12.09%, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Unpaid customer bills rose 61% while sales rose 12%. That can mean sales are being pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. The reported Decart deal is about competition in AI chips (general knowledge: it supports the cloud business). At the reported price it adds to cash spending, but it does not change this quarter's demand. The worker dispute over data centres and the New York City shipping-label complaint matter for sentiment and regulation, not for current results. What is not at risk: liquidity of 114.2B covers near-term needs. What is at risk: the stock's valuation if growth keeps slowing while spending stays high.

worth.text: No discounted-cash-flow value is possible because free cash flow is negative. So the only fair-value method is Amazon's own price-to-sales history (price divided by sales per share): 187.93 at the low end, 238.65 in the middle and 265.96 at the high end. At 255.39 the price is above the middle and below the top. Amazon's price-to-sales of 3.5 sits at the 62nd percentile of its own 5-year history. That is far below the peer median of 6.0, and 0.63 of the peers on a growth-adjusted basis. The gap between 'cheap versus peers' and 'fully priced versus its own history' depends on which yardstick applies. Earnings multiples look moderate: 20.7 times trailing earnings and 20.0 times this year's. But analysts expect next-year earnings of 10.67 per share, below 12.8 this year, so the multiple rises to 23.9. The filings flag that the price implies about 34% yearly growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. Note: the valuation summary in the data was computed at 246.82, before today's rise.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.0.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales is producing more profit.
Price-to-sales of 3.5 is well below the peer median of 6.0, and only 0.63 of peers on a growth-adjusted basis.
Revenue over the last 12 months reached 797.5B, up from 691.3B, and the next-year earnings estimate was revised up 1.4% in 30 days.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from +10.6B, and net debt stands at 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
Next-year earnings are estimated at 10.67 per share versus 12.8 this year, which lifts the forward P/E to 23.9, and operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 2–13%.

levels.what: Middle of the own-history value range, inside the 233.59–238.97 support zone. This is the main buy level.
The 200-day average, at the bottom of the strong 244.3–249.71 support zone (9 touches). A small first buy here only if the next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B.
Top of the own-history value range. No buying above it.

longterm.why: Today's rise took the price further above the 238.65 buy level, while the cash burn and slowing growth remain unresolved. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: At 255.39 the price is in the middle of its 251.93–258.08 zone, and resistance at 259.49–265.34 is within one typical day's move (the average true range, or typical daily move, is 10.38). The trend is a range with flat averages. No trade unless the price pulls back into 244.3–249.71 and holds, or closes above 265.34.

decision.timing: With no earnings date in the data, price levels set the timing. Options to 2026-12-18 price in a move of about 10.5% (priced off 246.82), and the largest open put positions sit at the 200 and 240 strikes.

change_mind: A filing showing 12-month free cash flow back above zero (it is -46.9B now), with operating margin holding at or above 13.09%, would turn the view to buy at 245.38.
Quarterly sales growth back above 16.61% would ease the slowdown concern; growth below 12.09% combined with operating margin back under 11.02% would move the view to avoid.
A close above 265.96 (top of the value range) would mean the price has left fair value, and the view would stay wait. A break below 233.59 would make 187.93 the next value reference.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because today's 3.47% rise to 255.39 moved the price further above the 238.65 buy level while 12-month free cash flow is still -46.9B.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Microsoft rebounds 1.65% to 492.5, back above support; hold, swing entry triggered

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and margins keep improving, but free cash flow has fallen while heavy spending continues, so the stock looks cheap against its own history and expensive on cash flow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold and add only lower. Swing: enter, because the price closed back above the 491.22 trigger set in the last note.
summary.act_at: Swing entry 491.22, stop 480.69, target 503.99; long-term add at 475.73

note.happening: Microsoft rose 1.65% to 492.5. That put it back above the top of its 486.0–491.22 support zone, a few days after it broke below that zone. The only news since the last note is a CNBC report of a government official warning of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages, and the report does not name Microsoft. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
note.business: The latest filing, dated 2026-10-28, shows a business that is still speeding up. Quarterly revenue grew 18.8% from a year earlier, compared with 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Analysts raised next-year earnings per share to 24.2, up 2.2% in 30 days. The weak point is cash. The gap between methods comes from the growth assumption: the bear case starts from analysts' 5% EPS growth, while the base and bull cases use the recent 15% sales growth. Margin matters too. If operating margin fell to 23%, the value would be 58.77, slightly above today's price. At 15% margin it would drop to 38.82.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 10% to 20% a year, close to the 12.4% the price implies, and operating margin does not fall much below 23%.

bull: Free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, and free cash flow is 22.87% of sales.
Price-to-sales of 4.8 sits at the 18th percentile of its own 5-year range and below the peer median of 6.5.
Share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each share owns more of the profits.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
Operating margin of 31.3% is at the top of its 5-year range; at 15% margin the value is only 38.82.
Analysts cut this quarter's EPS estimate 7.3% in 30 days, to 0.68 from 0.73.

levels.what: Value if operating margin falls to 23%. Small adds below it still carry a cushion even if margins fade.

swing.why: The trend is down, with lower highs and lower lows below every falling average. Resistance sits at 61.14–61.64 and 64.56–65.08, and no support level gives a place for a stop. No trade until a close above 65.08.

This quarter's revenue comes in below the 13.4B consensus while EPS estimates keep falling from 0.68: that would mean the slowdown is deepening, so adds stop.
